newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court upholds rules for importing sour cherries into the EU.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds rules for importing sour cherries into the EU.

text.p: The European Court of Justice validated on Thursday European Commission rules on the import of sour cherries into the Community.
The regulation was challenged by Lubella, a German cannery, after being charged with countervailing duties for importing sour cherries into Germany.
The court reviewed the regulation and found it adhered to principles of proportionality, protected legitimate expectations and adequately stated the reasons on which it was based.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: German)
"Common organization of the market in fruit and vegetables - Protective measures - Sour cherries"
Reference by the Finanzgericht des Landes Brandendurg (Germany) for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between
Konservenfabrik Lubella Friedrich Buker GmbH & Co.KG
on the validity of Community regulation (EEC) No 1932/93 of 16 July 1993 establishing protective measures as regards the import of sour cherries (OJ 1993 L 174, p. 35)

Consideration of the questions referred to the Court has disclosed no factor of such a kind as to affect the validity of Community regulation (EEC) No 1932/93 of 16 July 1993 establishing protective measures as regards the import of sour cherries.
